neighbours.label: the word just before an expected 'main / headquarters / central' (e.g. 'has its [headquarters]', 'is the [main]')
fire: The largest insurance firm in the region also has its headquarters in Hartford.
For most of the century, the old railway station was the main point of arrival for visitors.
Researchers suspect this gland is the body's master regulator of growth.
After the merger, the bank kept its headquarters in a tower downtown.
In that era the cathedral square was the central meeting place of the town.
Many people assume the heart is the brain's main source of signals, but that is wrong.
The software company moved its headquarters to Austin last spring.
The American Bar Association is the main professional body for lawyers in the country.
quiet: The largest insurance firm in the region also sold its old cars to a dealer in Hartford.
For most of the century, the railway station was painted green and white every few years.
Researchers suspect this gland is the body's least studied organ in small mammals.
After the merger, the bank lost several customers who had complained about fees.
In that era the cathedral square was often flooded during the spring rains.
Many people assume the heart beats faster when they are frightened, and that is right.
The software company hired forty engineers in Austin last spring.
The American Bar Association published a report on legal fees last year.

notes: Card: peaks on ' its', ' the', "'s" right before headquarters/main/master; the - pole's output promotes ' main', ' master', ' central', ' headquarters'. Near misses keep the determiner but the continuation is not a main/central/headquarters word.
